Commentary.Commentary: ... 4th Innings ...

The Sri Lankan second innings was just the way they would have wanted. Short and impactful. They lost a couple of wickets on Day 3 but they came out to bat today with a purpose in mind. They wanted to extend the lead as much as possible and they have extended it to over 400. Led once again by Dimuth Karunaratne and handy knocks by Pathum Nissanka and Niroshan Dickwella they scored 194. Will Sri Lankan bowlers run through the batting lineup or will Bangladesh show character and hang in there? We will find out...

Sri Lanka have declared and they are well and truly on top here. They have 436 runs in the bank and around 5 sessions to get 10 wickets to win this game. The pitch is starting to assist the spinners and it will be up to Praveen Jayawickrama and Ramesh Mendis to do the bulk of the damage. Bangladesh need to bat out of their skins to chase this one and it will be very interesting to see their approach with the bat.

... Day 4, Session 2 ...

Right then! Sri Lanka already have a lead of 414 runs. Will they declare in the next session or target 450? On the other hand, Bangladesh would look to bowl out Sri Lanka as quickly as they can in the next session. Join us for the second session in 40 minutes!

Coming to Bangladesh, their bowlers picked up 4 wickets but they needed a better performance in the first hour if they had to come back in the game. They gave many freebies. The spinners struggled a bit. In the second hour of this session, the bowlers bowled better. Saif Hassan broke the partnership between Karunaratne and Dhananjaya de Silva. He dismissed the Sri Lankan skipper. Mehidy Hasan got his second wicket in this innings as he dismissed Dhananjaya de Silva. Taijul Islam got his third wicket in this innings as he dismissed Nissanka. Taskin Ahmed did not get any wicket. However, they gave away too many easy runs and will be disappointed with that.

It has been an excellent session for Sri Lanka. They lost 4 wickets but they have got a good lead of over 400. Dimuth Karunaratne and Dhananjaya de Silva's partnership was crucial for them today. Karunaratne lost his wicket when he was on 66. Dhananjaya de Silva continued for a while but could not stay longer as he got out on 41. Dickwella and Nissanka started building a partnership. Nissanka played some good shots but perished early. Ramesh Mendis came and did well to support Dickwella. They did well to stay till the end of the session.

Pitch Report - Farveez Maharoof is down for the pitch report. He says that there is a rough area outside the off stump for the right-handers and the wicket looks similar to yesterday. Adds that it is slightly gloomy and that will also be a factor.

Hello and a warm welcome to Day 4 of this Test match. The first hour will be crucial as Bangladesh will look to pick up a few early wickets and put the hosts on the back foot and restrict them to a low score in their second innings. On the other hand, Sri Lanka will look to motor along and pile up runs to make sure that they can't lose this game.

Bangladesh have begun the second innings nicely with the ball, helped generously by Sri Lanka with two wickets. But they need to have a stupendously great Sunday to have a chance of coming back into this Test match. Day 4 will also have an early start and the proceedings begin at 0945 local (0415 GMT). However, if the forecast is to be believed, there is rain forecast throughout the day. Still, do join us. ADIOS! TAKE CARE!

Bangladesh began well with Tamim, Mominul and Rahim fighting hard. But once Rahim fell on the last ball before Tea, a procession followed. The visitors slipped from 214/3 to 251 all out, handing a big lead of 242 to the Lankans. Praveen Jayawickrama stood out for the home side, taking a 6-fer.

The day started with Sri Lanka intriguingly continuing to bat in spite of so much time lost due to bad weather. And then when they did, they declared at a time when Niroshan Dickwella was approaching his century. They eventually declared 7 short of 500 and then asked Bangladesh to respond.

Well, a moving day, as is rightly called in terms of Day 3 in Test cricket. Sri Lanka may have faltered towards the end, but overall, it is their game to lose now. A day where they stunned Bangladesh with the ball and have that ball in their own court.
